Subject: Dedicated capacity recap — Aurora Health (next steps)

Hi Sahil and Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — useful conversation. Quick recap of what we heard and the recommended next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of pain points we discussed:
- Throughput: 200–300 concurrent requests at peak for real-time clinical summarization workloads (avg 750 tokens).
- Isolation: PHI-sensitive data, need customer-dedicated GPUs and VPC isolation (no multi-tenant inference).
- Predictability: Need predictable latency SLOs and monthly committed capacity to control unit costs.

Goals / success criteria:
- 99.9% uptime SLA for inference endpoints.
- P50 latency < 150ms for 512-token responses during normal traffic; P95 under 400ms at peak.
- Data never leaves Aurora’s VPC; audit logs retained 13 months.

Redwood recommended configuration (based on today's load profile):
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB (reserved) with burst-to-shared pool for temporary spikes.
- Private deployment option (VPC peering + KMS integration) to meet PHI isolation and key control requirements.
- Autoscaling policy: vertical burst (short-term) + scheduled scale-up for predictable peak windows (weekday mornings).

Next steps / asks:
1) I attached a draft capacity plan (proposed_capacity_plan.xlsx) with estimated throughput and cost. Please review and flag any initial changes.
2) Can you confirm procurement timeline and whether Aurora requires an approved vendor questionnaire before legal review?
3) Technical deep-dive: propose Mon, Mar 24 or Tue, Mar 25 for a 30–45m session with your infra team + our infra/SEs.

I'll loop in Monica (our solutions lead) to coordinate the technical call and pull together an SLA / deployment-runbook draft.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite once we settle a time.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Hi Sahil — great questions. A few notes from product/ops perspective: 

- Burst model: the burst-to-shared pool is intended for short spikes (5–30 min typical). If bursts run longer than the configured threshold we can either (a) auto-scale additional reserved nodes (if scheduled) or (b) start charging at the burst rate in the plan. We'll capture exact burst thresholds in the SOW.
- Isolation: for Redwood Private we support a customer-managed VPC where the inference containers run in your subnet and keys are managed by your KMS; model weights are pulled into ephemeral encrypted local volumes that are not shared across customers. KV cache and model artifacts are destroyed on teardown and we provide audit logs. We can provide the architecture diagram in the technical call.
- SLA remedies: typical SLA in Dedicated is uptime SLA (credits) and a latency SLO with escalation contacts. We will draft the exact credit table for P95/P99 latency breaches and include escalation steps.

Monica, can you lead the deep-dive and bring an ops runbook + deployment diagram?

Rishi
